dossier.public_summary: The dip’s depth changes dramatically between sectors and between individual transits, with a few very deep outliers driving the signal. Odd and even transits also differ and the light curve prefers a grazing stellar eclipse. Together this is best explained as noise or blended variability, not a 1.4 Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Depth varies by factor ~40 (46, -35, -104, 834, -40, 550, -17, -28, 427, 1342, 234, 390, 1857 ppm), chi2 582.8 dof 13. This is not a steady astrophysical transit.

QLP p_constant 1.2286507432415214e-60 depth 437 ppm and SPOC 2-min p_constant 5.194120675564476e-47 depth 116 ppm both show significant intra-source variation, so it is not a calibration offset between sources.

Individual transits are highly inconsistent (chi2 1272.3462479095842 dof 25). Top 3 carry 0.725 of signal, outliers at 2559 ppm sigma 18.0, 2412 ppm sigma 17.0, 1540 ppm sigma 14.6, 1342 ppm sigma 13.8; most others near zero. Best fit achieved with 2-3 very deep events.

Odd 215.7 ppm vs even 339 ppm differ by 0.3638 (123.3 ppm) with depth ratio 1.6, and sector_oe_max_sigma 11.67 with 4 sectors over 3 same sign, consistent with a binary at 2x period (period_x2 24.6) not a planet.
If treated as undiluted 285.5 ppm it is planet-sized, but undiluted assumption is invalid because depth is transient and outlier-dominated.
Observed 4.997 h vs central 3.449 h and fit_b 0.9742 show a grazing-like duration with star_density_penalty 87.23, matching a stellar/eclipsing scenario rather than a planet transit.
